question: Does the four-group conditional writer frontier selected on the first v11 rows predict the unused v11 rows, and is L7H8 specifically useful only in the L9/MLP context?
selection_rule: From the completed 32-arm discovery factorial, choose the smallest subset whose worst task-mode pre-H3 squared residual is at most 0.125. This uniquely selects mask 30: L7H8 + L9H1/H4 + MLP7 + MLP9. Mask 31 is the fidelity comparator, mask 28 removes L7H8 from the selected context, and mask 4 is the known L9 baseline.
sealed_population: For each task and A1/A2 panel, skip the seven rows used by the discovery factorial and take the next seven jointly capable rows. No sealed activation or intervention outcome entered selection.

predictions.instrument: Authority, exact row disjointness, capability, response shapes, attention replay, base self-patch, finiteness, arm count, and price close.
predictions.frontier_predicts: Mask 30 has pre-H3 squared residual at most 0.20 with cosine at least 0.90 in all four task-mode cells and positive behavioral direction on at least 90% of rows.
predictions.beats_l9: Mask 30 reduces squared residual relative to mask 4 by at least 10% in at least three of four task-mode cells.
predictions.conditional_l7h8: Adding L7H8 (mask 28 to mask 30) reduces is/was mode-2 squared residual by at least 20%, while its signed marginal is not required to equal the failed singleton effect.
predictions.fidelity_no_worse: Mask 31's mean four-cell residual is no more than 5% above mask 30; L7H7 remains optional rather than necessary.

decision: All predictions yield a held-out conditional writer screen: L7H8 is licensed only as part of the L9/MLP context, not as a stable standalone shared mode writer. Failure of the conditional increment demotes L7H8 to construction-specific. Failure of the frontier kills the selected writer program without refitting or trying another subset on these rows.
